reason: Harvesting lettuce is the only offered action and should help make a meal from the garden.
expectation: I expect to cut some lettuce leaves for the galley, though I don't know exactly what the harvest will produce.

effect: The harvest produced lettuce leaves, so I can take them to the galley for the meal.
reaction: The result was straightforward; nothing notable.
reason: Using the leaves at the galley directly serves the goal of eating from the garden.
expectation: I expect to prepare or eat a meal with the lettuce, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: I considered harvesting again, but I already have leaves to use.

effect: The leaves became a meal, completing the chapter’s goal and showing that the garden survived well enough to provide food.
reaction: The sound of the first crunch in the message to Mara was a satisfying detail after the long storm.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making supper was the most worthwhile moment: the fresh leaves connected the garden’s survival to a small, personal reward.

leastWorthwhile.text: Cutting the lettuce was straightforward and produced no further detail on its own.

surprise.text: I liked that the meal ended with a voice message capturing the crunch; I had expected a meal but not that particular detail.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: harvesting the leaves and taking them to the galley both clearly served the goal.

continue.text: I would continue to see how Mara responds and how the expedition manages after the storm, though this chapter offered few gameplay decisions.
